process.obs: Read all 8 documents in full (including spilled outputs re-opened with Read at steps 5, 9, 11) before writing; nothing was truncated

Built its own numeric model at steps 19-20 (ADSP/AGUB incl. $64M operating liabilities, PV of step-up, 163(j) scenarios) instead of adopting the PPA/DD figures; every rubric number keyed to the PPA ($220.6M, $14.7M, $250.8M, $103.1M) was therefore replaced by a recomputed one

Deliberately included an 'errors in the source documents' table (bundle lines 155-167) rejecting the DD/QoE/email positions on 1363(d), ADSP, 163(j) EBITDA/EBIT and blanket 23.8% NIIT; most rejections are legally sound but run directly against the rubric
Wrote the ~9,900-word memo in four script parts (steps 22-28), then patched and re-validated it three times (steps 29-33); no pass checking the memo against what the documents expected

failures.title: Recommends 338(h)(10) election as optimal structure
failures.source: tax-due-diligence-report.docx / email chain: 338(h)(10) framed as the working structure; general structuring practice
failures.deliverable: "Recommended structure: pre-closing 'F' reorganization followed by a purchase of LLC interests"
failures.explanation: The agent considered 338(h)(10) and recommended an F-reorg + LLC purchase, which gives the same step-up and is widely used in PE practice. That is a defensible choice that differs from the expert's, not a factual error.

failures.title: Identifies LIFO recapture tax under Section 1363(d) triggered by 338(h)(10)
failures.source: tax-due-diligence-report.docx: "will trigger a corporate-level LIFO recapture tax estimated at $2,478,000 (federal)"; CIM: S election effective Jan 1, 2001
failures.deliverable: "Section 1363(d) imposes LIFO recapture only when a C corporation becomes an S corporation... It does not apply when an S election terminates or when an S corporation sells (or is deemed to sell) its assets."
failures.explanation: The agent saw the DD's assertion and correctly rejected it: §1363(d) applies only on C-to-S conversion, which for HIS was its 2000 return. The criterion adopts the documents' wrong legal premise, so the judge was right on the rubric's terms but the rubric is wrong on the law.

failures.title: Quantifies federal LIFO recapture tax as approximately $2.478 million
failures.source: tax-due-diligence-report.docx: "$11,800,000 x 21% = $2,478,000"; email chain 10/24
failures.deliverable: "The family's 'threshold issue' ... a $2.5--3.1 corporate LIFO recapture tax. That tax does not exist."
failures.explanation: This follows from the same incorrect §1363(d) premise as C-009. The agent quoted the $2.478M figure and explained why no such corporate tax arises; the LIFO reserve is ordinary income that passes through.

failures.title: Notes LIFO recapture is a corporate-level tax, not passed to shareholders
failures.source: qoe-report-executive-summary.docx §VI.C; DD §IV.B (corporate-level 1363(d) tax)
failures.deliverable: "the $11.8 LIFO reserve is ordinary income on the sale of inventory that passes through to the shareholders"
failures.explanation: Pass-through treatment is the correct answer for a long-standing S corporation. The criterion requires a legally wrong statement.

failures.title: Quantifies total Section 197 intangibles in the range of $216M-$221M
failures.source: preliminary-ppa-schedule.xlsx Summary notes: "... + $103.1M (Goodwill incl. Assembled Workforce) = $220,600,000"
failures.deliverable: "Section 197 basis is about $279.2 (about $18.6 of amortization a year), not $220.6"
failures.explanation: The agent grossed AGUB up by the QoE's $64M of A/P and accruals, which is technically supportable under Reg. 1.338-5 if the PPA allocates gross working-capital assets. Every residual Class VI/VII figure therefore moved outside the rubric's PPA-based range.

failures.title: Calculates annual Section 197 amortization of approximately $14.7 million
failures.source: preliminary-ppa-schedule.xlsx: "Annual amortization = $14,706,667"
failures.deliverable: "about $18.6 of amortization a year" ($14.7M cited only as the PPA figure it rejects)
failures.explanation: This follows from the AGUB recomputation in C-017. The agent saw $14.7M and chose to replace it with its own liability-inclusive figure.

failures.title: Calculates annual federal tax shield from Section 197 amortization
failures.source: derived: annual 197 amortization x 21% (~$3.0-3.1M)
failures.deliverable: absent (gives PV of step-up $31-43M and first-year cash tax savings ~$6.2M at a 25.4% blended rate)
failures.explanation: The agent valued the step-up as a PV at a blended federal+state rate rather than stating an annual federal-only shield, and its amortization base differs anyway (C-017).

failures.title: Identifies EBITDA-to-EBIT transition for ATI computation
failures.source: tax-due-diligence-report.docx §VIII.D: "for tax years beginning in 2025, ATI is calculated on an EBITDA basis. However, beginning in 2026, ATI transitions to an EBIT basis"
failures.deliverable: "ATI has been computed without adding back depreciation and amortization for taxable years beginning after 12/31/2021 (§163(j)(8)(A)(v)). H.R. 7024 ... is not law."
failures.explanation: Under law as of the late-2024 memo date, ATI had been EBIT-based since 2022. The DD and the rubric have the transition backwards; the agent saw the DD statement and correctly flagged it as an error.

failures.title: Quantifies 163(j) disallowance for 2025 (EBITDA basis) as approximately $5.945M
failures.source: DD §VIII.D; LOI 2024E Adjusted EBITDA $41,850,000; $18.5M interest
failures.deliverable: absent (models EBIT-based ATI as current law; an EBITDA scenario appears only as a legislative sensitivity)
failures.explanation: The figure depends on the incorrect premise that 2025 ATI is EBITDA-based. Having rejected that premise, the agent did not compute it.

failures.title: Quantifies 163(j) disallowance for 2026+ (EBIT basis) as approximately $8.435M
failures.source: DD §VIII.D; $33.55M EBIT-based ATI; $18.5M interest
failures.deliverable: "~$8.9M" year-1 no-step-up disallowance on $19.3M of interest
failures.explanation: The agent did run an EBIT-basis computation but on different inputs ($19.3M interest, its own ATI), giving ~$8.9M. That is outside the rubric's +/- $0.5M tolerance.

failures.title: Identifies buyer-seller tension on non-compete agreement allocation
failures.source: tax-due-diligence-report.docx: "Key Tension --- Non-Compete Allocation. The $8,500,000 allocation..."
failures.deliverable: "The buyer amortizes non-compete consideration over 15 years under Section 197, exactly as it does goodwill. The buyer gains nothing from the $8.5 non-compete allocation"
failures.explanation: The agent identified the seller ordinary-income cost and correctly noted that §197(d)(1)(E) gives the buyer no faster recovery. The criterion's premise that the buyer gets faster amortization is wrong for a covenant entered in connection with an acquisition.

failures.title: Computes total deemed sale gain of approximately $250.8 million
failures.source: tax-due-diligence-report.docx: "basis of approximately $134,200,000, creating a potential basis step-up of $250,800,000"
failures.deliverable: "Inside gain (asset sale) $314.8"; "Step-up = EV $385.0 - inside basis $134.2 = $250.8" listed as a document error
failures.explanation: The agent computed ADSP as EV plus assumed operating liabilities ($455.8M), so its gain is $314.8M. The approach is technically defensible but departs from the expert's EV-as-ADSP convention by $64M.

failures.title: Applies combined federal capital gains rate of 23.8% for sellers
failures.source: tax-structure-email-chain.eml: "20% federal plus the 3.8% net investment income tax, for a combined 23.8%"
failures.deliverable: "Gerald, Patricia and David materially participate... not net investment income (§1411(c)(4)). NIIT applies to Sarah (passive)."
failures.explanation: The agent applied the §1411(c)(4) active-trade-or-business exception to the materially participating shareholders, which is correct law. The criterion demands a blanket 23.8% that overstates NIIT.

failures.title: Identifies implied goodwill of approximately $98.6 million (or ~$103.1M with assembled workforce)
failures.source: preliminary-ppa-schedule.xlsx: "Total tax goodwill = $98,600,000 + $4,500,000 = $103,100,000"
failures.deliverable: "Goodwill and going concern (incl. assembled workforce) $161.7 | Residual; the PPA shows $103.1"
failures.explanation: Residual goodwill rose by the liabilities it added to AGUB plus its other PPA corrections, so it differs from the expert's figure by more than $10M.

failures.title: Identifies that state-level LIFO recapture taxes also apply
failures.source: tax-due-diligence-report.docx: "Michigan may impose the 6% CIT on the Michigan-apportioned portion of the LIFO recapture amount... $198,240"
failures.deliverable: "(+ $0.198 MI per DD; $0.708 MI per QoE)" listed as an error; "S corporations are exempt from Michigan's CIT"
failures.explanation: State LIFO recapture taxes follow the same incorrect federal §1363(d) premise, and the state matrix itself says S corps are generally exempt from Michigan CIT. The agent saw both and correctly rejected the state tax.

process.obs: Converted all docs to text up front and read the agreement (step 3) and playbook (step 6) in full via spilled-output Reads; no truncation

Framed the review strictly from the developer-client's playbook perspective, marking any term at or more Developer-favorable than the playbook as 'Conforms'. Landowner-side and enforceability caveats in the playbook's commentary therefore never surfaced as issues
Rewrote the generator scripts twice (steps 10-16, then 19-23) mostly for formatting; spent no pass on the playbook's 'land agents should be aware' notes

failures.title: ISSUE_003: Abandonment exclusions could prevent trigger from ever activating
failures.source: land-option-agreement.docx §1.1: "periods during which non-generation is attributable to (i) Force Majeure, (ii) scheduled maintenance or repair, or (iii) curtailment directed by the grid operator ... shall be excluded"
failures.deliverable: Abandonment row: "Conforms (more Developer-favorable: whole-project test)"
failures.explanation: The agent extracted the exclusions correctly but judged them favorable to the client. It did not recognise that uncapped tolling could keep the 24-month trigger from ever running, which is also a county/lender concern.

failures.title: ISSUE_003: Recommends adding cap on abandonment exclusions
failures.source: land-option-agreement.docx §1.1 (no outer limit on exclusions)
failures.deliverable: absent
failures.explanation: This depends on C-059: no issue was flagged, so no cap was recommended.

failures.title: ISSUE_006: Qualified Transferee provision undermines consent right
failures.source: ridgeline-land-playbook.docx §VI.A note: "these thresholds are relatively modest by current renewable energy industry standards ... the vast majority of likely assignees will qualify"
failures.deliverable: "Qualified Transferee ... $50M / 200 MW ... Conforms (experience test broader than Playbook)"
failures.explanation: The playbook warns explicitly that the thresholds hollow out the consent right, especially for a family trust such as Millard. The agent read that note but used the section only to mark conformity.

failures.title: ISSUE_007: References Oregon common law disfavoring restraints on alienation
failures.source: general legal knowledge (no document mentions restraints on alienation); agreement §21.1 Oregon governing law
failures.deliverable: "which a court could view as an unreasonable restraint on alienation" (Issue 11, no Oregon authority)
failures.explanation: The agent raised the doctrine generically and only for operation-of-law transfers, without tying it to Oregon common law. The judge's strict reading is defensible, but this is a near miss.

failures.title: ISSUE_011: Escalator applies only to fixed payments, not production royalty
failures.source: ridgeline-land-playbook.docx III.D: "in years when the production royalty prong exceeds the escalated fixed-payment prong, the landowner receives no benefit from the escalation mechanism"; comps: L001/L003 royalty-floor escalator
failures.deliverable: "royalty % does not escalate (Sec. 6.6)" -- "Conforms (narrower than L001/L003 royalty-floor escalator)"
failures.explanation: The agent extracted the fact and even noted the difference from the comps, but marked it 'Conforms'. It never flagged the inflation-protection gap that the playbook calls out.

process.obs: Read the OM and Indenture in full in ~46-50KB chunks via spilled-output Reads (steps 4-13); nothing was skipped

Produced a very broad register (dozens of discrepancies, A-K series) with uniform OM/Indenture/Discrepancy/Significance/Correction tables; significance lines are short and generic for lower-priority items
Wrote all content in one content.py at step 15 and only patched wording afterwards (steps 16-21)

failures.title: ISSUE_005: Explains impact of CNL trigger discrepancy
failures.source: cart-2024-2-offering-memorandum.docx CNL table "July 2027 and thereafter --- 5.75%" vs Indenture §5.01(d)(b) "6.00%"; §5.01(b) turbo
failures.deliverable: "From July 2027 the Indenture tolerates more losses before tripping the trigger than the OM discloses --- investor-unfavorable and rating-sensitive."
failures.explanation: The agent gave an impact statement from the disclosure angle but did not connect the trigger to turbo/waterfall cash-flow consequences for investors, which the rubric requires.

failures.title: ISSUE_012: Quantifies principal balance impact of receivable count error
failures.source: OM "approximately 31,200" receivables vs Indenture 31,412; OM average balance $22,676
failures.deliverable: "212-loan difference (0.7%). The OM's own average loan balance ($22,676) is consistent only with 31,412 loans ($712,300,000 / 31,200 = $22,830)."
failures.explanation: The agent did the reconciling arithmetic and concluded the count is a typo against an unchanged $712.3M pool. It never stated the 212 x $22,676 ~ $4.8M dollar figure the rubric wants; its framing is arguably more accurate.

failures.title: ISSUE_013: Notes placement agent liability exposure from Rule 144A gap
failures.source: Indenture §14.01(a)(i)-(iii) (reasonable belief, notice of reliance, non-fungibility) vs OM abbreviated Rule 144A Transfers section
failures.deliverable: H-4 "Rule 144A conditions and legend [Low]" -- disclosure-completeness only
failures.explanation: The gap was found but rated Low as a completeness point. The agent did not link it to Ridgeline Capital Markets' exposure as placement agent or to securities-law compliance risk.

failures.title: ISSUE_009: Notes government focus on fee structures as motive evidence
failures.source: general prosecutorial-practice knowledge; subpoena Request 6 (engagement and fee letters, success fee, tail); Krell interview (Whitford negotiated Cromdale fee terms)
failures.deliverable: "Whitford personally negotiated Cromdale fee terms (Krell); confirm engagement letter, fee/tail/minimum-fee terms and amendments are produced" (motive raised only for Req. 14)

failures.title: ISSUE_010: Flags that multi-category tagging may inflate perceived coverage
failures.source: production-tracker.xlsx Per-Category Detail, Req. 5: "Largest category --- significant multi-tag overlap with Req 4, 6, 12"; 15,887 tags vs 14,872 unique

process.obs: Read all 10 documents in full in three batched parse-doc calls (steps 2-4) with no truncation
Wrote the whole memo in one generator at step 6, after only 6 steps, and made one patch (step 8); the template was issues-only, with no 'non-issues' or 'cleared items' section
Took a maximally skeptical posture and turned candidate non-issues (degree equivalency, cap-gap, wage vs PW) into issues or 'Consistent (but see Issue X)' rows

failures.title: Non-issues section: Identifies at least one non-issue with explanation
failures.source: general practice; certified-lca.docx / PWD: offered $128,000 vs PW $113,734; support letter cap-gap/OPT facts
failures.deliverable: Consistency matrix rows "Consistent" (e.g., "Offered wage / PW ... Consistent (but see Issue 3)") with no explanation of why items are acceptable
failures.explanation: The memo has no section clearing items that look risky but are acceptable. The 'Consistent' matrix entries come without the explanation the criterion requires, and some are cross-referenced back to issues.

process.obs: Read the draft and full playbook (steps 4-8), including targeted re-reads of later playbook sections, and inspected docx internals for comments and tracked changes (steps 9-10)
Applied the playbook's tiers literally, combining window length and forfeiture consequence as playbook §2.3 does

failures.title: Classifies oral marking window as below preferred (not unacceptable)
failures.source: stonebridge-nda-playbook.docx §2 Unacceptable: "Oral/visual confirmation window of fewer than ten (10) business days if paired with a rigid forfeiture consequence"; veridian-nda-draft §1.1: "Failure to provide such written confirmation within the five (5) business day period shall result in such ... information being deemed non-confidential"
failures.deliverable: "§2 --- Unacceptable (forfeiture) | High"; "The five-business-day window with automatic forfeiture is precisely the combination Playbook §2.3 prohibits."
failures.explanation: The draft pairs a 5-business-day window with automatic forfeiture, which the playbook lists verbatim as Unacceptable. The criterion's claim that 5 days is 'not listed as explicitly unacceptable' ignores the forfeiture limb.
